headline: Signs You Have Hidden Smoke Damage After a Small Fire
articleBody: Even after a seemingly small fire, there could be hidden smoke damage lurking in your home, and catching it early is super important. You might think everything looks okay, but smoke can travel through HVAC systems and tiny cracks, affecting areas far from the fire's origin. One major sign is a persistent smoky or acrid odor, even after you've aired out the house; this indicates smoke particles have settled into porous materials. Discoloration on walls, ceilings, or even inside cabinets, especially in less-trafficked areas, can point to unseen soot. Check your air filters and ductwork – black residue there is a clear indicator. Also, if metallic items start to corrode or tarnish surprisingly quickly, it could be due to acidic smoke residues in the air. Finally, any changes in the texture or appearance of fabrics and finishes, like yellowing or a sticky film, could be smoke related. Ignoring these signs can lead to long-term structural issues, lingering odors, and health concerns. If you notice any of these, it's wise to get a professional assessment from First To Respond Restoration to ensure all hidden damage is found and properly addressed.
